I baked three fruit cakes earlier this month. I had hoped to use brandy but I didnt have any on hand. This was my first time making fruit cake so I decided to try three different liquors. One is Grand Marnier, one is Limoncello, and one is Triple Sec. Will they be terrible? Did I screw up? If I did can my cakes be saved? I've been feeding them each a couple spoonfuls each week for three weeks now.
Are flavored liquors okay in fruit cakes?
I have pretty good success with Rum. If you don't get anybody with direct experience I'd suggest tasting each and seeing what you think.

Rum helps a cake rise in addition to flavourful. I would expect the liquor flavored cakes to be a little denser in terms of crumb texture. Otherwise , they'll still be tasty. The limoncello one should be particularly fresh and zippy.
That's a relief! The main thing I was worried about was the flavor in the liquor being overwhelming.
It'll be stronger because of the sugar content but the variety of flavors you used should off set that.
